thread:
jordan: Heads up — getting a handful of tls handshake anomalies from eu-west -> ap-south services since last deploy. Noticed the cipher fingerprint changed on the proxy side (looks like a server-side profile rollback?) and session-ticket entropy warnings in the logs. Also saw an RBAC change for keystore roles earlier today in infra PR #4821. Any correlation?

miles: Yikes. Can you paste the probe output? I can run quick scans.

jordan: pasted snippet: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect service.prod.eu-west.internal:443 -servername svc
---
Protocol  : TLSv1.3
Cipher    : TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
Session-ID: <empty>
Session-Ticket: <present but 0-length?>
verify return:1
---
```
logs show: `session-ticket: insufficient-entropy` repeated for several backends.

security-bot: [alert] 2025-01-21T13:47:02Z - TLS anomaly rate spike (eu-west -> ap-south) — 46 failed handshakes in 10m. Alert ID: tls-entropy-17532

diane: Was the keystore RBAC change the one that removed the `ptls-reader` role from the proxy service account? I remember an infra rollback of broad roles earlier today.

miles: Yes — PR 4821 removed `ptls-reader` from the `proxy-deploy` SA and added a narrower `keystore-fetcher` role. The intent was least privilege but I did not think it would affect session-ticket unwrap.

sre-oncall: Quick triage steps: 1) confirm the proxy can call KMS/unwrap with the new role (iam simulate) 2) check rotator logs for unwrap errors 3) fallback to cached ticket path if unwrap fails.

jordan: iam simulate shows 403 on `kms:Decrypt` from the proxy node in ap-south. So role change definitely impacted unwrap calls. That explains `insufficient-entropy` message — when we can't unwrap server ticket we fall back and then logs complain.

diane: That 403 is the root cause for the handshake churn then. Two questions: how widespread, and service impact?

miles: Initial scan: ~12 proxies across eu-west/ap-south and one regional rotator reported unwrap denies. Latency spikes for affected routes ~+120ms p50 and increased TLS failures for long-lived clients. Not full outage but noisy.

security-bot: [incident] Created incident INC-2025-045 (severity: elevated). Links: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2025-045

sre-oncall: Proposed mitigation: re-add `kms:Decrypt` permission to proxy SA (short-term) + update rotator to respect the new `keystore-fetcher` pattern (long-term). We should also add a fast fail path in proxy: if unwrap fails, use a local ephemeral cache and reduce logging severity.

diane: Approve quick revert for safety. Who can cut the IAM revert?

miles: I'll push a minimal IAM patch to re-grant `kms:Decrypt` scoped to the proxy keystore resource and roll. ETA 15m.

jordan: Also recommend we add a post-deploy check: run an `openssl s_client` probe and a KMS unwrap test as part of the proxy helmpostinstall check.

sre-oncall: Agree. Add these checks to the deploy pipeline — gating for RBAC changes touching keystores. I'll open a follow-up on the oncall board.

diane: For compliance/audit: capture the exact PR, the IAM diff, and the timeline of observed TLS anomalies. Security needs the event log for the change window + proof that revert fixed it.

miles: Will attach PR link and audit entries here after rollback. Also will enable extended audit logging for KMS unwraps for 24h to ensure no silent failures.

jordan: After revert, I re-ran the probe — `Cipher: TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384`, `Session-Ticket: present (length ok)`, no entropy warnings. Latency returned to baseline.

sre-oncall: Closing mitigation: rollback IAM applied, rotator/keystore team to produce two tickets: 1) implement least-privilege IAM with explicit unwrap path and test harness; 2) add deploy-time KMS unwrap probe + `openssl` handshake smoke test per region.

diane: Thanks everyone. Action owners: miles (IAM rollback + audit logs) / rotator team (design least-privilege path + tests) / sre-oncall (pipeline gating). Please update INC-2025-045 with confirmations and timeline.

miles: rolling now. Will post results. :thumbsup:

jordan: posting small postmortem draft to #postmortems after we confirm the timing. Main lessons: RBAC changes touching keystores must be validated with live unwrap tests; session-ticket unwrap failures manifest as entropy logs, not obvious 403s in TLS output.

security-bot: [update] INC-2025-045 status -> mitigated at 2025-01-21T14:02:10Z.

miles: rollback completed, KMS unwrap success now. Verified access logs show `Decrypt` calls succeeded.

diane: Good. Capture remediation steps and schedule a runbook change.

sre-oncall: I'll add a runbook entry: "RBAC keystore changes — validate unwrap and handshake per-region; fallback cache policy; audit log window".

jordan: thanks all, closing thread after postmortem doc is published.
